record.paper_title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: How should incentive mechanisms, including contract-theory, game-theory, auction-theory, and crowdsourcing mechanisms, be designed to motivate self-interested people and mobile users to share relevant information or change behavior for social distancing tasks such as keeping safe distances, contact tracing, crowd detection, location or movement sharing, stay-at-home compliance, and self-isolation?

evidence.quote: Due to the people’s self-interested/selfish nature characteristics in their daily life [311] (especially during the pandemic outbreak), incentive mechanisms can be very helpful in encouraging people to accept or share relevant information to enable new social distancing methods.
Inspired by the aforementioned works, we can consider the contract theory-based method along with D2D communications to encourage people to keep distances from other people/crowds.
To further drive people away from high-density public places, one can also consider incentive mechanisms for better social distancing efficiency (especially for the people with their mobile devices).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a population of N self-interested agents, each equipped with a mobile device, who can participate in one or more social-distancing tasks T = {keeping safe physical distances, contact tracing, crowd detection, sharing location or movement data, stay-at-home compliance, self-isolation}. Each agent i has a private type θ_i ∈ Θ_i (capturing cost of effort, privacy valuation, risk perception, mobility pattern) drawn from a known prior, and chooses an action/effort level a_i ∈ A_i that produces a utility u_i(a_i, a_{-i}, θ_i, r_i) where r_i is a reward from a planner (e.g. a public-health authority or platform). The planner has a budget B and seeks to maximize a social-welfare or epidemic-mitigation objective W(a_1,…,a_N) (such as expected reduction in transmission rate or expected number of high-density contacts avoided) subject to: (i) individual rationality u_i ≥ 0, (ii) incentive compatibility (truthful reporting of θ_i and/or honest task execution), (iii) budget feasibility Σ r_i ≤ B, and (iv) privacy guarantees on shared data.

Design and analyze incentive mechanisms in the following four families that achieve these constraints and characterize their optimal performance:
1. Contract-theory mechanisms: design a menu of contracts {(effort level, reward)} indexed by reported type, optimal under asymmetric information about θ_i, possibly combined with device-to-device (D2D) communication for distance-keeping tasks.
2. Game-theory mechanisms: specify a non-cooperative game among agents (and possibly a planner) and identify equilibria (Nash, Bayesian, or Stackelberg) that implement the desired social-distancing behavior, analyzing the price of anarchy versus the social optimum.
3. Auction-theory mechanisms: design truthful auctions (e.g., VCG-type or reverse auctions) for procuring sensing, contact-tracing, or location-sharing services from mobile users while minimizing payment subject to coverage constraints.
4. Crowdsourcing mechanisms: design task allocation and reward rules to recruit mobile users for crowd-detection or movement-sharing tasks, ensuring quality of contributed data and worker participation.

Provide, for each family, a formal model, a mechanism, and a proof of incentive compatibility, individual rationality, budget feasibility, and an approximation guarantee for W relative to the first-best optimum.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed as an open research direction in a survey on social-distancing technologies, has not been settled. Subsequent literature (2020–2024) has proposed partial mechanisms—e.g., contract-theoretic and Stackelberg-game incentives for contact tracing apps, reverse auctions for mobile crowdsensing of crowd density—but a unified framework covering all four mechanism families across all listed social-distancing tasks with provable optimality has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists incentive-mechanism design for social-distancing participation as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Original framing identifies this as an open research direction.
